I, Yahweh, have spoken. Surely this I will do to all this wicked congregation who have gathered together against me. In this wilderness they will come to an end, and there they will die.”
And the men whom Moses sent to explore the land, who returned and made the whole congregation grumble against him by bringing a bad report about the land,
the men who brought the bad report about the land died by a plague before Yahweh.
Of those men who went to explore the land, only Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh remained alive.
When Moses told these words to all the Israelites, the people mourned greatly.
They rose early in the morning and went up to the top of the hill country, saying, “Here we are. We will go up to the place that Yahweh has promised, for we have sinned.”{h}
But Moses said, “Why are you transgressing the command of Yahweh? It will not succeed.
Do not go up, for Yahweh is not among you, so that you will not be struck down before your enemies.
For the Amalekites and the Canaanites are there before you, and you will fall by the sword. Because you have turned back from following Yahweh, Yahweh will not be with you.”
But they presumed to go up to the top of the hill country, although neither the ark of the covenant of Yahweh nor Moses departed from the camp.
Then the Amalekites and the Canaanites who lived in that hill country came down and struck them and crushed them as far as Hormah.{i}

notes.text: Hebrew “their shadow,” that is, the protection of their gods.
In the traditional Hebrew text the first letter of the word for “be great” is written larger than normal, a scribal feature with no certain meaning.
Hebrew khesed, covenant loyalty and love. Verses 18–19 echo Exodus 34:6–7.
Hebrew yam suf, “Sea of Reeds.” Here it probably refers to the Gulf of Aqaba. See the note at Exodus 10:19.
Hebrew “lifted my hand,” a gesture of swearing an oath.
Hebrew “bear your whoredoms,” a common biblical image for unfaithfulness to God.
Or “what it means to have me against you.” The Hebrew word is rare.
At this point and after verse 45 the Samaritan Pentateuch adds material drawn from Deuteronomy 1–2. See the note at 10:10.
Hormah means “destruction” or “devoted to destruction.” Compare 21:3.

verses.text: Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to the Israelites and say to them, ‘When you come into the land where you are to live, which I am giving you,

and you make an offering by fire to Yahweh from the herd or from the flock, a burnt offering or a sacrifice, to fulfill a vow or as a freewill offering or at your appointed festivals, to make a pleasing aroma to Yahweh,
then the one who brings his offering is to present to Yahweh a grain offering of about 2 quarts of fine flour mixed with about 1 quart of oil.{a}
You are also to prepare about 1 quart of wine for the drink offering with the burnt offering or for the sacrifice, for each lamb.
For a ram you are to prepare as a grain offering about 4 quarts of fine flour mixed with about 1⅓ quarts of oil.{b}
And for the drink offering you are to present about 1⅓ quarts of wine, a pleasing aroma to Yahweh.
When you prepare a young bull as a burnt offering or a sacrifice, to fulfill a vow, or as peace offerings to Yahweh,
then one is to present with the young bull a grain offering of about 6 quarts of fine flour mixed with about 2 quarts of oil.{c}
And you are to present for the drink offering about 2 quarts of wine, as an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to Yahweh.
“‘This is how it is to be done for each bull or ram, or for each male lamb or young goat.
According to the number that you prepare, so you are to do with each one, according to their number.
Every native-born Israelite is to do these things in this way, in presenting an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to Yahweh.
And if a foreigner is living with you, or anyone who is among you throughout your generations, and he wants to present an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to Yahweh, he is to do as you do.
For the assembly, there is to be one statute for you and for the foreigner who lives with you, a permanent statute throughout your generations. As you are, so the foreigner is to be before Yahweh.
One law and one rule is to apply to you and to the foreigner who lives with you.’”
Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to the Israelites and say to them, ‘When you come into the land to which I am bringing you
and you eat of the bread of the land, you are to present a contribution to Yahweh.
From the first of your dough{d} you are to present a loaf as a contribution. Like a contribution from the threshing floor, so you are to present it.
From the first of your dough you are to give to Yahweh a contribution throughout your generations.
“‘But if you unintentionally fail and do not keep all these commandments that Yahweh has spoken to Moses,
all that Yahweh has commanded you through Moses, from the day that Yahweh gave commandment and onward throughout your generations,

then, if it was done unintentionally, without the knowledge of the congregation, the whole congregation is to offer one young bull as a burnt offering, a pleasing aroma to Yahweh, with its grain offering and its drink offering according to the rule, and one male goat as a sin offering.

The priest is to make atonement for the whole congregation of the Israelites, and they will be forgiven, because it was a mistake, and they have brought their offering, an offering by fire to Yahweh, and their sin offering before Yahweh for their mistake.
The whole congregation of the Israelites will be forgiven, and the foreigner who lives among them, because the whole people was involved in the mistake.
“‘If one person sins unintentionally, he is to offer a female goat a year old as a sin offering.
The priest is to make atonement before Yahweh for the person who has made a mistake, when he sins unintentionally, to make atonement for him, and he will be forgiven.
You are to have one law for the one who acts unintentionally, both for the native among the Israelites and for the foreigner who lives among them.
But the person who acts with a high hand,{e} whether native or foreigner, is blaspheming Yahweh, and that person is to be cut off from among his people.
Because he has despised the word of Yahweh and has broken his commandment, that person is to be completely cut off. His iniquity will be on him.’”
While the Israelites were in the wilderness, they found a man gathering wood on the Sabbath day.
Those who found him gathering wood brought him to Moses and Aaron and to the whole congregation.
They put him in custody, because it had not been made clear what should be done to him.
Then Yahweh said to Moses, “The man must be put to death. The whole congregation is to stone him with stones outside the camp.”
So the whole congregation brought him outside the camp and stoned him with stones, and he died, as Yahweh had commanded Moses.
Yahweh said to Moses,
“Speak to the Israelites and tell them to make tassels{f} on the corners of their garments throughout their generations, and to put a cord of blue{g} on the tassel of each corner.

It will be a tassel for you to look at and remember all the commandments of Yahweh and do them, and not follow after your own heart and your own eyes, which you are inclined to go after in unfaithfulness.
So you will remember and do all my commandments, and be holy to your God.
I am Yahweh your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God. I am Yahweh your God.”

notes.text: Hebrew “a tenth of fine flour mixed with a quarter of a hin of oil,” about 2.2 liters of flour and 0.9 liter of oil. The tenth is a tenth of an ephah; an ephah was about three-fifths of a bushel (22 liters), and a hin about 1 gallon (3.7 liters). Standards varied. So also with the wine in verse 5.
Hebrew “two-tenths of fine flour mixed with a third of a hin of oil,” about 4.4 liters of flour and 1.2 liters of oil. So also with the wine in verse 7.
Hebrew “three-tenths of fine flour mixed with half a hin of oil,” about 6.6 liters of flour and 1.9 liters of oil. So also with the wine in verse 10.
Or “coarse meal.” The Hebrew word ‘arisah is uncertain.
That is, defiantly and deliberately.
Hebrew tsitsit, a tassel or fringe.
Hebrew tekhelet, a blue or violet dye made from murex shellfish.

verses.text: Now Korah son of Izhar, son of Kohath, son of Levi, took men,{a} together with Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, and On son of Peleth, sons of Reuben.{b}
They rose up before Moses, together with two hundred fifty men of the Israelites, leaders of the congregation, chosen from the assembly, men of renown.

They assembled against Moses and against Aaron and said to them, “You have gone too far! For all the congregation is holy, every one of them, and Yahweh is among them. Why then do you exalt yourselves above the assembly of Yahweh?”
When Moses heard it, he fell on his face.

Then he said to Korah and all his company, “In the morning Yahweh will make known who is his, and who is holy, and will bring him near to himself. The one whom he chooses he will bring near to himself.
Do this: take censers, Korah and all his company,
and tomorrow put fire in them and put incense on them before Yahweh. The man whom Yahweh chooses, he is the holy one. You have gone too far, sons of Levi!”
And Moses said to Korah, “Hear now, you sons of Levi:

Is it too small a thing for you that the God of Israel has separated you from the congregation of Israel, to bring you near to himself, to do the service of the tabernacle of Yahweh and to stand before the congregation to minister to them,
and that he has brought you near, and all your brothers the sons of Levi with you? Would you seek the priesthood also?
Therefore it is against Yahweh that you and all your company have gathered together. As for Aaron, who is he, that you grumble against him?”
Moses sent to call Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, but they said, “We will not come up.
Is it a small thing that you have brought us up out of a land flowing with milk and honey to kill us in the wilderness, that you must also make yourself a prince over us?
Moreover, you have not brought us into a land flowing with milk and honey, nor given us an inheritance of fields and vineyards. Will you gouge out the eyes of these men?{c} We will not come up.”
Moses was very angry and said to Yahweh, “Do not respect their offering. I have not taken a single donkey from them, and I have not harmed one of them.”
And Moses said to Korah, “You and all your company, be present before Yahweh tomorrow, you and they and Aaron.
Each of you take his censer and put incense on it, and each of you bring his censer before Yahweh, two hundred fifty censers; you also, and Aaron, each his censer.”
So each man took his censer, put fire in them, laid incense on them, and stood at the entrance of the tent of meeting with Moses and Aaron.
Korah assembled the whole congregation against them at the entrance of the tent of meeting. And the glory of Yahweh appeared to the whole congregation.
Yahweh spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,
“Separate yourselves from among this congregation, so that I may consume them in a moment.”
But they fell on their faces and said, “O God, the God of the spirits of all flesh, shall one man sin, and will you be angry with the whole congregation?”
Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to the congregation, saying, ‘Get away from around the dwelling of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram.’”
Then Moses rose and went to Dathan and Abiram, and the elders of Israel followed him.
He spoke to the congregation, saying, “Depart, please, from the tents of these wicked men, and touch nothing of theirs, or you will be swept away in all their sins.”
So they got away from around the dwelling of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram. Dathan and Abiram came out and stood at the entrance of their tents, with their wives, their sons, and their little ones.
And Moses said, “By this you will know that Yahweh has sent me to do all these works, and that it has not been of my own accord.{d}
If these men die as all people die, or if they are visited by the fate of all people, then Yahweh has not sent me.

But if Yahweh creates something new, and the ground opens its mouth and swallows them up with all that belongs to them, and they go down alive into Sheol,{e} then you will know that these men have despised Yahweh.”
As soon as he had finished speaking all these words, the ground under them split apart.
The earth opened its mouth and swallowed them up, with their households and all the people who belonged to Korah{f} and all their goods.
So they and all that belonged to them went down alive into Sheol, and the earth closed over them, and they perished from the midst of the assembly.
All Israel who were around them fled at their cry, for they said, “The earth might swallow us up!”
And fire came out from Yahweh and consumed the two hundred fifty men who were offering the incense.
Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,{g}
“Tell Eleazar son of Aaron the priest to take up the censers out of the blaze, and scatter the fire far away, for they have become holy.

As for the censers of these men who sinned at the cost of their lives, let them be made into hammered plates as a covering for the altar, for they presented them before Yahweh, and they became holy. So they will be a sign to the Israelites.”
So Eleazar the priest took the bronze censers that those who were burned had presented, and they were hammered out as a covering for the altar,

to be a reminder to the Israelites, so that no outsider who is not of the descendants of Aaron should come near to burn incense before Yahweh, lest he become like Korah and his company, as Yahweh had said to him through Moses.
But on the next day the whole congregation of the Israelites grumbled against Moses and against Aaron, saying, “You have killed the people of Yahweh.”
When the congregation had assembled against Moses and against Aaron, they turned toward the tent of meeting, and the cloud covered it, and the glory of Yahweh appeared.
Moses and Aaron came to the front of the tent of meeting,
and Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,
“Get away from the midst of this congregation, so that I may consume them in a moment.” And they fell on their faces.

Moses said to Aaron, “Take your censer, put fire on it from the altar, lay incense on it, and carry it quickly to the congregation and make atonement for them, for wrath has gone out from Yahweh. The plague has begun.”
So Aaron took it as Moses had said and ran into the midst of the assembly. And the plague had already begun among the people. He put on the incense and made atonement for the people.
He stood between the dead and the living, and the plague was stopped.
Those who died in the plague were fourteen thousand seven hundred, besides those who died in the affair of Korah.
Aaron returned to Moses at the entrance of the tent of meeting, when the plague was stopped.

notes.text: Or “took action,” or “became insolent.” The Hebrew has no object, and the meaning is uncertain.
Korah perhaps means “bald.” Izhar means “shining.” Dathan is of uncertain meaning. Abiram means “my father is exalted.” On means “strength” or “wealth.” Peleth perhaps means “swiftness.”
That is, will you blind them to what you are doing?
Hebrew “from my heart.”
Sheol is the realm of the dead, pictured as beneath the earth. So also in verse 33.
According to 26:11, the sons of Korah did not die.
In the Hebrew text, verses 36–50 are numbered 17:1–15.

verses.text: Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,{a}
“Speak to the Israelites and take from them staffs, one for each father’s house, from all their leaders according to their fathers’ houses, twelve staffs. Write each man’s name on his staff.
Write Aaron’s name on the staff of Levi. For there is to be one staff for the head of each father’s house.
You are to deposit them in the tent of meeting before the testimony, where I meet with you.
And the staff of the man whom I choose will sprout. So I will stop the grumblings of the Israelites, which they grumble against you, from coming before me.”
Moses spoke to the Israelites. All their leaders gave him staffs, one for each leader, according to their fathers’ houses, twelve staffs. And the staff of Aaron was among their staffs.
And Moses deposited the staffs before Yahweh in the tent of the testimony.
On the next day Moses went into the tent of the testimony, and the staff of Aaron for the house of Levi had sprouted. It had put out buds, produced blossoms, and borne ripe almonds.
Then Moses brought out all the staffs from before Yahweh to all the Israelites. They looked, and each man took his staff.
Yahweh said to Moses, “Put back the staff of Aaron before the testimony, to be kept as a sign for the rebels, so that you may put an end to their grumblings against me, lest they die.”
Moses did so. As Yahweh commanded him, so he did.
The Israelites said to Moses, “Look, we perish, we are undone, all of us are undone!
Everyone who comes near, who comes near to the tabernacle of Yahweh, will die. Are we all to perish?”

notes.text: In the Hebrew text, verses 1–13 are numbered 17:16–28.

verses.text: Yahweh said to Aaron, “You and your sons and your father’s house with you are to bear the iniquity connected with the sanctuary, and you and your sons with you are to bear the iniquity connected with your priesthood.

Bring with you also your brothers, the tribe of Levi, the tribe of your father, so that they may be joined to you{a} and serve you while you and your sons with you are before the tent of the testimony.
They are to keep guard over you and over the whole tent, but they must not come near the vessels of the sanctuary or the altar, lest both they and you die.
They are to be joined to you and keep guard over the tent of meeting for all the service of the tent, and no outsider is to come near you.
You are to keep guard over the sanctuary and over the altar, so that there may never again be wrath on the Israelites.
I myself have taken your brothers the Levites from among the Israelites. They are a gift to you, given to Yahweh, to do the service of the tent of meeting.

But you and your sons with you are to guard your priesthood in everything concerning the altar and what is inside the veil, and you are to serve. I give you your priesthood as a gift of service, and any outsider who comes near is to be put to death.”

Then Yahweh spoke to Aaron, “I myself have given you charge of the contributions made to me, all the holy things of the Israelites. I have given them to you as a portion{b} and to your sons as a permanent due.

This is to be yours from the most holy things, kept back from the fire: every offering of theirs, every grain offering, every sin offering, and every guilt offering that they render to me, is to be most holy for you and for your sons.
You are to eat it as a most holy thing. Every male may eat it. It is to be holy to you.

This also is yours: the contribution of their gift, all the wave offerings of the Israelites. I have given them to you, and to your sons and daughters with you, as a permanent due. Everyone in your house who is clean may eat it.
All the best of the oil and all the best of the new wine and of the grain, the firstfruits of what they give to Yahweh, I have given to you.
The first ripe fruits of all that is in their land, which they bring to Yahweh, are to be yours. Everyone in your house who is clean may eat it.
Everything devoted{c} in Israel is to be yours.

Everything that opens the womb of all flesh, which they present to Yahweh, both of people and of animals, is to be yours. Nevertheless, you must surely redeem the firstborn of people, and you are to redeem the firstborn of unclean animals.
Their redemption price, from a month old, you are to fix at about 2 ounces of silver,{d} by the sanctuary standard.

But the firstborn of a cow, or the firstborn of a sheep, or the firstborn of a goat, you must not redeem. They are holy. You are to sprinkle their blood on the altar and burn their fat as an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to Yahweh.
But their flesh is to be yours, just as the breast that is waved and the right thigh are yours.

All the holy contributions that the Israelites present to Yahweh I have given to you, and to your sons and daughters with you, as a permanent due. It is a covenant of salt{e} forever before Yahweh for you and for your descendants with you.”
And Yahweh said to Aaron, “You are to have no inheritance in their land, nor any portion among them. I am your portion and your inheritance among the Israelites.
“To the descendants of Levi I have given every tithe in Israel as an inheritance, in return for their service that they do, the service of the tent of meeting.
The Israelites must no longer come near the tent of meeting, lest they bear sin and die.

But the Levites are to do the service of the tent of meeting, and they are to bear their iniquity. It is to be a permanent statute throughout your generations. They are to have no inheritance among the Israelites.

For the tithe of the Israelites, which they present as a contribution to Yahweh, I have given to the Levites as an inheritance. Therefore I have said to them that they are to have no inheritance among the Israelites.”
Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

“Speak to the Levites and say to them, ‘When you take from the Israelites the tithe that I have given you from them as your inheritance, you are to present a contribution from it to Yahweh, a tithe of the tithe.
Your contribution will be counted to you as though it were grain from the threshing floor and the full yield of the winepress.
So you also are to present a contribution to Yahweh from all your tithes that you receive from the Israelites, and from them you are to give Yahweh’s contribution to Aaron the priest.
From all the gifts to you, you are to present every contribution due to Yahweh, from all the best of them, the holy part from them.’
Therefore you are to say to them, ‘When you have presented the best of it, it will be counted to the Levites as the produce of the threshing floor and as the produce of the winepress.
You may eat it in any place, you and your households, for it is your wages in return for your service in the tent of meeting.
You will bear no sin because of it, when you have presented the best of it. But you must not profane the holy things of the Israelites, lest you die.’”

notes.text: The Hebrew verb for “be joined” (lavah) sounds like the name Levi. So also in verse 4.
Or “because of the anointing.” The Hebrew word is uncertain.
Hebrew kherem, something irrevocably given over to God, either for destruction or for the sanctuary’s use.
Hebrew “five shekels,” about 57 grams. A shekel was about 0.4 ounce (11.5 grams); standards varied. The text adds that the shekel is twenty gerahs; a gerah was one-twentieth of a shekel.
That is, a permanent and binding covenant. Salt, which preserves, was used in sealing agreements.

verses.text: Yahweh spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,
“This is the statute of the law that Yahweh has commanded: Tell the Israelites to bring you a red heifer{a} without defect, in which there is no blemish, and on which a yoke has never come.
You are to give it to Eleazar the priest, and it is to be taken outside the camp and slaughtered in his presence.
Eleazar the priest is to take some of its blood with his finger and sprinkle some of its blood toward the front of the tent of meeting seven times.
Then the heifer is to be burned in his sight. Its skin, its flesh, and its blood, with its dung, are to be burned.
The priest is to take cedarwood, hyssop, and scarlet yarn and throw them into the midst of the burning heifer.
Then the priest is to wash his clothes and bathe his body in water, and afterward he may come into the camp, but the priest will be unclean until evening.
The one who burns it is to wash his clothes in water and bathe his body in water, and he will be unclean until evening.

A man who is clean is to gather up the ashes of the heifer and deposit them outside the camp in a clean place. They are to be kept for the congregation of the Israelites for the water for impurity.{b} It is a purification from sin.
The one who gathers the ashes of the heifer is to wash his clothes and will be unclean until evening. This is to be a permanent statute for the Israelites and for the foreigner who lives among them.
“Whoever touches the dead body of any person will be unclean seven days.

He is to purify himself with the water on the third day and on the seventh day, and then he will be clean. But if he does not purify himself on the third day and on the seventh day, he will not become clean.

Whoever touches a dead person, the body of anyone who has died, and does not purify himself, defiles the tabernacle of Yahweh, and that person is to be cut off from Israel. Because the water for impurity was not thrown on him, he is unclean. His uncleanness is still on him.
“This is the law when someone dies in a tent: everyone who comes into the tent and everyone who is in the tent will be unclean seven days.
And every open vessel that has no cover fastened on it is unclean.
Whoever in the open field touches someone who was killed with a sword, or who died naturally, or a human bone, or a grave, will be unclean seven days.
For the unclean person they are to take some of the ashes of the burned purification offering, and fresh water{c} is to be added to them in a vessel.

Then a clean person is to take hyssop and dip it in the water and sprinkle it on the tent, on all the vessels, on the people who were there, and on whoever touched the bone, or the slain, or the dead, or the grave.

The clean person is to sprinkle the unclean on the third day and on the seventh day. On the seventh day he is to purify him, and he is to wash his clothes and bathe in water, and in the evening he will be clean.

“But the one who is unclean and does not purify himself, that person is to be cut off from the midst of the assembly, because he has defiled the sanctuary of Yahweh. The water for impurity has not been thrown on him; he is unclean.
This is to be a permanent statute for them. The one who sprinkles the water for impurity is to wash his clothes, and the one who touches the water for impurity will be unclean until evening.
Whatever the unclean person touches will be unclean, and the person who touches it will be unclean until evening.”

notes.text: Or “a red cow.” The Hebrew word parah denotes a young female of the herd; its reddish-brown color may evoke blood.
Hebrew me niddah, “water of impurity,” water used to remove impurity. So also in verses 13, 20, and 21.
Hebrew “living water,” that is, water from a flowing source.

verses.text: The Israelites, the whole congregation, came into the Wilderness of Zin in the first month (in March–April),{a} and the people stayed at Kadesh. Miriam died there and was buried there.
There was no water for the congregation, and they assembled against Moses and against Aaron.
The people quarreled with Moses and said, “If only we had died when our brothers died before Yahweh!
Why have you brought the assembly of Yahweh into this wilderness, that we and our livestock should die here?
And why have you made us come up out of Egypt to bring us to this evil place? It is no place for grain or figs or vines or pomegranates, and there is no water to drink.”
Then Moses and Aaron went from the presence of the assembly to the entrance of the tent of meeting and fell on their faces. And the glory of Yahweh appeared to them.
Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

“Take the staff, and assemble the congregation, you and Aaron your brother, and speak to the rock before their eyes to yield its water. So you will bring water out of the rock for them and give drink to the congregation and their livestock.”
Moses took the staff from before Yahweh, as he had commanded him.
Moses and Aaron gathered the assembly together in front of the rock, and he said to them, “Hear now, you rebels: shall we bring water for you out of this rock?”
Then Moses lifted up his hand and struck the rock with his staff twice, and water came out abundantly, and the congregation drank, and their livestock.

But Yahweh said to Moses and Aaron, “Because you did not believe in me, to treat me as holy in the eyes of the Israelites, therefore you will not bring this assembly into the land that I have given them.”
These are the waters of Meribah,{b} where the Israelites quarreled with Yahweh, and he showed himself holy among them.{c}
Moses sent messengers from Kadesh to the king of Edom: “Thus says your brother Israel: You know all the hardship that has come upon us,
how our fathers went down to Egypt, and we lived in Egypt a long time, and the Egyptians dealt harshly with us and our fathers.
And when we cried to Yahweh, he heard our voice and sent an angel{d} and brought us out of Egypt. Now we are at Kadesh, a city on the edge of your territory.

Please let us pass through your land. We will not pass through field or vineyard, or drink water from a well. We will go along the King’s Highway.{e} We will not turn aside to the right or to the left until we have passed through your territory.”
But Edom said to him, “You shall not pass through me, or I will come out with the sword against you.”
The Israelites said to him, “We will go up by the highway, and if we drink any of your water, I and my livestock, then I will pay for it. Let me only pass through on foot, nothing more.”
But he said, “You shall not pass through.” And Edom came out against them with a large force and a strong hand.
So Edom refused to let Israel pass through his territory, and Israel turned away from him.
They set out from Kadesh, and the Israelites, the whole congregation, came to Mount Hor.
Yahweh spoke to Moses and Aaron at Mount Hor, on the border of the land of Edom, saying,
“Aaron is to be gathered to his people, for he is not to enter the land that I have given to the Israelites, because you both rebelled against my command at the waters of Meribah.
Take Aaron and Eleazar his son and bring them up to Mount Hor.
Strip Aaron of his garments and put them on Eleazar his son. Aaron is to be gathered to his people and will die there.”
Moses did as Yahweh commanded. They went up to Mount Hor in the sight of the whole congregation.
Moses stripped Aaron of his garments and put them on Eleazar his son, and Aaron died there on the top of the mountain. Then Moses and Eleazar came down from the mountain.
When the whole congregation saw that Aaron had died, all the house of Israel wept for Aaron thirty days.{f}

notes.text: The first month of the spring-start religious calendar, Abib (later Nisan); the dates fall in different parts of March and April from year to year because the months were lunar. The year is not stated; it is usually taken to be the fortieth year after the exodus (compare 33:38).
Meribah means “quarreling.” Compare Exodus 17:7.

The Hebrew verb for “he showed himself holy” (yiqqadesh) echoes the name Kadesh. At this point the Samaritan Pentateuch adds material drawn from Deuteronomy 3:24–28, in which Moses pleads to enter the land. The Dead Sea Scroll 4QNumᵇ preserves a similar expansion. See the note at 10:10.
Or “a messenger.”
The ancient main road east of the Jordan, running north to south from Damascus to the Gulf of Aqaba.
According to 33:38, Aaron died on the first day of the fifth month of the fortieth year (in July–August).

verses.text: When the Canaanite, the king of Arad, who lived in the Negev, heard that Israel was coming by the way of Atharim,{a} he fought against Israel and took some of them captive.
And Israel made a vow to Yahweh and said, “If you will indeed give this people into my hand, then I will devote their cities to destruction.”{b}
Yahweh listened to the voice of Israel and gave over the Canaanites, and they devoted them and their cities to destruction. So the name of the place was called Hormah.{c}
They set out from Mount Hor by the way of the Red Sea, to go around the land of Edom. And the people became impatient on the way.
The people spoke against God and against Moses, “Why have you brought us up out of Egypt to die in the wilderness? For there is no bread and no water, and we loathe this worthless food.”
Then Yahweh sent fiery serpents{d} among the people, and they bit the people, so that many people of Israel died.
The people came to Moses and said, “We have sinned, for we have spoken against Yahweh and against you. Pray to Yahweh, that he take away the serpents from us.” So Moses prayed for the people.
And Yahweh said to Moses, “Make a fiery serpent and set it on a pole. Everyone who is bitten, when he sees it, will live.”
So Moses made a bronze serpent{e} and set it on a pole. And if a serpent bit anyone, he would look at the bronze serpent and live.
The Israelites set out and camped at Oboth.
They set out from Oboth and camped at Iye-abarim,{f} in the wilderness that is opposite Moab, toward the sunrise.
From there they set out and camped in the Valley of Zered.

From there they set out and camped on the other side of the Arnon, which is in the wilderness that extends from the border of the Amorites. For the Arnon is the border of Moab, between Moab and the Amorites.
Therefore it is said in the Book of the Wars of Yahweh,{g} “Waheb in Suphah,{h} and the valleys of the Arnon,
and the slope of the valleys that extends to the seat of Ar, and leans to the border of Moab.”
From there they went to Beer.{i} That is the well of which Yahweh said to Moses, “Gather the people together, and I will give them water.”
Then Israel sang this song: “Spring up, O well! Sing to it!
The well that the princes dug, that the nobles of the people delved, with the scepter and with their staffs.” And from the wilderness they went to Mattanah,{j}
and from Mattanah to Nahaliel, and from Nahaliel to Bamoth,
and from Bamoth to the valley that is in the country of Moab, by the top of Pisgah, which looks down on the wasteland.{k}
Then Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites, saying,
“Let me pass through your land. We will not turn aside into field or vineyard. We will not drink water from a well. We will go by the King’s Highway until we have passed through your territory.”
But Sihon would not allow Israel to pass through his territory. Sihon gathered all his people together and went out against Israel to the wilderness, and came to Jahaz and fought against Israel.
And Israel struck him with the edge of the sword and took possession of his land from the Arnon to the Jabbok, as far as the Ammonites, for the border of the Ammonites was strong.{l}
Israel took all these cities, and Israel settled in all the cities of the Amorites, in Heshbon and in all its villages.{m}
For Heshbon was the city of Sihon king of the Amorites, who had fought against the former king of Moab and taken all his land out of his hand, as far as the Arnon.
Therefore the ballad singers say, “Come to Heshbon, let it be built; let the city of Sihon be established.
For fire went out from Heshbon, flame from the city of Sihon. It consumed Ar of Moab, the lords of the heights of the Arnon.{n}
Woe to you, Moab! You are undone, people of Chemosh!{o} He has made his sons fugitives and his daughters captives to an Amorite king, Sihon.
But we shot them down; Heshbon has perished, as far as Dibon, and we laid waste as far as Nophah, which reaches to Medeba.”{p}
So Israel settled in the land of the Amorites.
Moses sent to spy out Jazer, and they captured its villages and drove out the Amorites who were there.
Then they turned and went up by the way of Bashan. And Og king of Bashan came out against them, he and all his people, to battle at Edrei.
But Yahweh said to Moses, “Do not fear him, for I have given him into your hand, with all his people and his land. You will do to him as you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived at Heshbon.”
So they struck him and his sons and all his people, until no survivor was left to him. And they took possession of his land.

notes.text: Or “the way of the spies.” The meaning of Atharim is uncertain.
Hebrew kharam, to devote irrevocably to God, usually by destruction.
Hormah means “destruction.”
Hebrew seraf, “burning one,” probably for the burning pain of the bite. The same word describes the seraphim in Isaiah 6:2.
Hebrew nekhash nekhoshet, a wordplay: “a serpent of bronze.” King Hezekiah later destroyed it because it had become an object of worship (2 Kings 18:4). Compare John 3:14–15.

Iye-abarim means “ruins of Abarim” or “ruins of the regions beyond.” At several points in this chapter (after verses 11, 12, 20, and 21) the Samaritan Pentateuch adds material drawn from Deuteronomy 2. See the note at 10:10.
A lost collection of poems about Israel’s battles, known only from this quotation.
The meaning of the Hebrew is uncertain. Waheb and Suphah may be place names; the line lacks a verb, since the quotation begins mid-sentence.
Beer means “well.”
Mattanah means “gift.” Nahaliel means “valley of God.” Bamoth means “heights.”
Or “Jeshimon.”
The Septuagint reads “for Jazer was the border of the Ammonites.”
Hebrew “daughters.”
Or “the high places of the Arnon.”
Chemosh was the national god of Moab.
The meaning of verse 30 is uncertain. The Septuagint reads “fire” (Hebrew ’esh) in place of “which” (’asher), a reading many scholars prefer, giving “and fire was kindled as far as Medeba.”

verses.text: Then the Israelites set out and camped in the plains of Moab beyond the Jordan at Jericho.{a}
Now Balak son of Zippor{b} saw all that Israel had done to the Amorites.
And Moab was in great dread of the people, because they were many. Moab was filled with fear because of the Israelites.
And Moab said to the elders of Midian, “This horde will now lick up everything around us, as an ox licks up the grass of the field.” Balak son of Zippor was king of Moab at that time.

He sent messengers to Balaam son of Beor{c} at Pethor, which is near the River,{d} in the land of the people of his kin,{e} to call him, saying, “A people has come out of Egypt. They cover the face of the earth, and they are settled opposite me.

Now come, please, curse this people for me, since they are too mighty for me. Perhaps I will be able to defeat them and drive them out of the land. For I know that whomever you bless is blessed, and whomever you curse is cursed.”
So the elders of Moab and the elders of Midian departed with the fees for divination in their hand. They came to Balaam and spoke to him the words of Balak.
He said to them, “Stay here tonight, and I will bring back word to you, as Yahweh speaks to me.” So the princes of Moab stayed with Balaam.
And God came to Balaam and said, “Who are these men with you?”
Balaam said to God, “Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, has sent to me, saying,
‘Look, the people who have come out of Egypt cover the face of the earth. Now come, curse them for me. Perhaps I will be able to fight against them and drive them out.’”
God said to Balaam, “You must not go with them. You must not curse the people, for they are blessed.”
So Balaam rose in the morning and said to the princes of Balak, “Go to your own land, for Yahweh has refused to let me go with you.”
So the princes of Moab rose and went to Balak and said, “Balaam refuses to come with us.”
Once again Balak sent princes, more numerous and more honorable than these.
They came to Balaam and said to him, “Thus says Balak son of Zippor: ‘Please let nothing hinder you from coming to me,
for I will surely honor you greatly, and whatever you say to me I will do. Come, please, curse this people for me.’”
But Balaam answered and said to the servants of Balak, “Even if Balak were to give me his house full of silver and gold, I could not go beyond the command of Yahweh my God, to do less or more.
So now, please stay here tonight also, so that I may know what more Yahweh will say to me.”
And God came to Balaam at night and said to him, “If the men have come to call you, rise, go with them. But only the word that I speak to you, that you are to do.”
So Balaam rose in the morning, saddled his donkey, and went with the princes of Moab.
But God’s anger burned because he went, and the angel of Yahweh{f} took his stand in the road as an adversary{g} against him. Now he was riding on his donkey, and his two servants were with him.

The donkey saw the angel of Yahweh standing in the road with his drawn sword in his hand. So the donkey turned aside out of the road and went into the field. And Balaam struck the donkey to turn her back onto the road.
Then the angel of Yahweh stood in a narrow path between the vineyards, with a wall on this side and a wall on that side.
When the donkey saw the angel of Yahweh, she pressed herself against the wall and pressed Balaam’s foot against the wall. So he struck her again.
Then the angel of Yahweh went ahead and stood in a narrow place, where there was no way to turn either to the right or to the left.
When the donkey saw the angel of Yahweh, she lay down under Balaam. Balaam’s anger burned, and he struck the donkey with his staff.
Then Yahweh opened the mouth of the donkey, and she said to Balaam, “What have I done to you, that you have struck me these three times?”
Balaam said to the donkey, “Because you have made a fool of me. I wish I had a sword in my hand, for then I would kill you.”
The donkey said to Balaam, “Am I not your donkey, on which you have ridden all your life to this day? Have I ever been in the habit of treating you this way?” And he said, “No.”
Then Yahweh opened the eyes of Balaam, and he saw the angel of Yahweh standing in the road with his drawn sword in his hand. And he bowed down and fell on his face.
The angel of Yahweh said to him, “Why have you struck your donkey these three times? Look, I have come out as an adversary, because your way is reckless{h} before me.
The donkey saw me and turned aside before me these three times. If she had not turned aside from me, surely by now I would have killed you and let her live.”
Balaam said to the angel of Yahweh, “I have sinned, for I did not know that you stood in the road against me. Now therefore, if it is evil in your eyes, I will turn back.”
The angel of Yahweh said to Balaam, “Go with the men, but speak only the word that I tell you.” So Balaam went on with the princes of Balak.
When Balak heard that Balaam was coming, he went out to meet him at Ir-moab,{i} on the border formed by the Arnon, at the edge of the territory.
Balak said to Balaam, “Did I not send to you urgently to call you? Why did you not come to me? Am I not able to honor you?”
Balaam said to Balak, “Here I have come to you! Am I now able to speak anything at all? The word that God puts in my mouth, that I must speak.”
Then Balaam went with Balak, and they came to Kiriath-huzoth.{j}
And Balak sacrificed oxen and sheep and sent some to Balaam and to the princes who were with him.
In the morning Balak took Balaam and brought him up to Bamoth-baal,{k} and from there he saw the edge of the people.

notes.text: Hebrew “beyond the Jordan of Jericho,” that is, on the east side of the Jordan, opposite Jericho.
Balak perhaps means “devastator.” Zippor means “bird.”

Balaam perhaps means “devourer” or “the clan brings forth.” Beor means “burning.” A plastered wall inscription from about 800 BC found at Deir ‘Alla in Jordan tells of a seer named “Balaam son of Beor” who received a vision from the gods at night.
That is, the Euphrates.
Or “in the land of the Amawites,” a people known from ancient inscriptions. The Samaritan Pentateuch, the Syriac, and the Vulgate read “the land of the Ammonites.”
Or “the messenger of Yahweh,” a heavenly being who speaks and acts for Yahweh, at times as Yahweh himself. So throughout this chapter. Compare Exodus 3:2.
Hebrew satan, “adversary” or “opponent.” So also in verse 32.
The meaning of the Hebrew is uncertain; perhaps “perverse” or “headlong.”
Or “the city of Moab.”
Kiriath-huzoth means “city of streets.”
Bamoth-baal means “high places of Baal.”

verses.text: Balaam said to Balak, “Build for me here seven altars, and prepare for me here seven bulls and seven rams.”
Balak did as Balaam had said. Balak and Balaam offered a bull and a ram on each altar.
And Balaam said to Balak, “Stand beside your burnt offering, and I will go. Perhaps Yahweh will come to meet me, and whatever he shows me I will tell you.” And he went to a bare height.{a}
God met Balaam, and Balaam said to him, “I have arranged the seven altars and have offered a bull and a ram on each altar.”
And Yahweh put a word in Balaam’s mouth and said, “Return to Balak, and this is what you are to say.”
So he returned to him, and there he was, standing beside his burnt offering, he and all the princes of Moab.
And Balaam took up his discourse{b} and said, “From Aram Balak has brought me, the king of Moab from the mountains of the east: ‘Come, curse Jacob for me, and come, denounce Israel!’
How can I curse whom God has not cursed? How can I denounce whom Yahweh has not denounced?
For from the top of the crags I see him, from the hills I behold him. Here is a people dwelling alone, not counting itself among the nations!
Who can count the dust of Jacob, or number the fourth part{c} of Israel? Let me die the death of the upright, and let my end be like his!”
Balak said to Balaam, “What have you done to me? I took you to curse my enemies, and look, you have done nothing but bless them.”
He answered and said, “Must I not take care to speak what Yahweh puts in my mouth?”
Balak said to him, “Please come with me to another place, from which you may see them. You will see only the edge of them and will not see them all. Curse them for me from there.”
So he took him to the field of Zophim,{d} to the top of Pisgah, and built seven altars and offered a bull and a ram on each altar.
Balaam said to Balak, “Stand here beside your burnt offering, while I meet Yahweh over there.”
And Yahweh met Balaam and put a word in his mouth and said, “Return to Balak, and this is what you are to say.”
So he came to him, and there he was, standing beside his burnt offering, and the princes of Moab with him. And Balak said to him, “What has Yahweh spoken?”
And Balaam took up his discourse and said, “Rise, Balak, and hear; give ear to me, son of Zippor:
God is not a man, that he should lie, or a son of man, that he should change his mind. Has he said, and will he not do it? Or has he spoken, and will he not fulfill it?
Look, I have received a command to bless; he has blessed, and I cannot revoke it.
He has not beheld misfortune in Jacob, nor has he seen trouble in Israel.{e} Yahweh their God is with them, and the shout of a king is among them.
God brings them out of Egypt; he is like the horns of the wild ox{f} for them.
For there is no enchantment against Jacob, no divination against Israel.{g} Now it will be said of Jacob and of Israel, ‘What has God done!’
Look, a people rising up like a lioness, and like a lion it lifts itself up. It does not lie down until it has devoured the prey and drunk the blood of the slain.”
Balak said to Balaam, “Do not curse them at all, and do not bless them at all.”
But Balaam answered Balak, “Did I not tell you, ‘All that Yahweh speaks, that I must do’?”
Balak said to Balaam, “Come, please, I will take you to another place. Perhaps it will be right in the eyes of God that you may curse them for me from there.”
So Balak took Balaam to the top of Peor, which overlooks the wasteland.
Balaam said to Balak, “Build for me here seven altars and prepare for me here seven bulls and seven rams.”
And Balak did as Balaam had said, and offered a bull and a ram on each altar.

notes.text: The meaning of the Hebrew word shefi is uncertain; it may mean a bare hill or “alone.”
Hebrew mashal, a word used for proverbs, parables, taunts, and oracles. So also in verse 18 and in chapter 24.
Or “the dust clouds.” The Hebrew word rova‘ is uncertain. The Septuagint reads “the families”; some ancient versions read “the multitudes.”
Zophim means “watchers” or “lookouts.”
Or “No one has seen iniquity in Jacob, or mischief in Israel.”
Or “the strength of a wild ox.” The meaning of the Hebrew to‘afot is uncertain.
Or “in Jacob … in Israel,” meaning that Israel does not practice divination.

verses.text: When Balaam saw that it pleased Yahweh to bless Israel, he did not go, as at other times, to look for omens, but set his face toward the wilderness.
Balaam lifted up his eyes and saw Israel camping tribe by tribe. And the Spirit of God came upon him,
and he took up his discourse and said, “The oracle of Balaam son of Beor, the oracle of the man whose eye is opened,{a}
the oracle of him who hears the words of God, who sees the vision of the Almighty,{b} falling down, with his eyes uncovered:
How beautiful are your tents, O Jacob, your dwellings, O Israel!
Like valleys that stretch out, like gardens beside a river, like aloes that Yahweh has planted, like cedar trees beside the waters.
Water will flow from his buckets, and his seed will be in many waters.{c} His king will be higher than Agag,{d} and his kingdom will be exalted.
God brings him out of Egypt; he is like the horns of the wild ox for him. He will devour the nations, his adversaries, and break their bones in pieces and pierce them through with his arrows.
He crouched, he lay down like a lion, and like a lioness; who will rouse him? Blessed is everyone who blesses you, and cursed is everyone who curses you.”
Then Balak’s anger burned against Balaam, and he struck his hands together. Balak said to Balaam, “I called you to curse my enemies, and look, you have done nothing but bless them these three times.
So now flee to your own place. I said that I would surely honor you, but Yahweh has kept you back from honor.”
Balaam said to Balak, “Did I not also tell your messengers whom you sent to me,
‘Even if Balak were to give me his house full of silver and gold, I could not go beyond the command of Yahweh, to do either good or bad of my own will. What Yahweh speaks, that I will speak’?
And now, I am going to my people. Come, I will advise you what this people will do to your people in the latter days.”
And he took up his discourse and said, “The oracle of Balaam son of Beor, the oracle of the man whose eye is opened,
the oracle of him who hears the words of God, and knows the knowledge of the Most High,{e} who sees the vision of the Almighty, falling down, with his eyes uncovered:

I see him, but not now; I behold him, but not near. A star will come out of Jacob, and a scepter{f} will rise out of Israel. It will crush the forehead{g} of Moab and break down all the sons of Sheth.{h}
Edom will be a possession; Seir also, his enemies, will be a possession, while Israel does valiantly.
One from Jacob will exercise dominion and destroy the survivors of the city.”
Then he looked on Amalek and took up his discourse and said, “Amalek was the first of the nations, but his end is destruction.”
And he looked on the Kenites and took up his discourse and said, “Enduring is your dwelling place, and your nest is set in the rock.{i}
Nevertheless, Kain will be burned when Asshur takes you away captive.”{j}
And he took up his discourse and said, “Alas, who will live when God does this?{k}
But ships will come from the coast of Kittim{l} and will afflict Asshur and afflict Eber, and he too will come to destruction.”
Then Balaam rose and went back to his place. And Balak also went his way.

notes.text: Or “closed.” The meaning of the Hebrew shetum is uncertain. So also in verse 15.
Hebrew Shaddai, a name of God of uncertain meaning, traditionally rendered “the Almighty.” So also in verse 16.
The meaning of the line is uncertain. The Septuagint reads, “A man will come out of his seed, and he will rule over many nations.”
Agag was a king of the Amalekites; compare 1 Samuel 15:8. The Septuagint and some other ancient witnesses read “Gog.”
Hebrew ‘Elyon.

Hebrew shevet, “scepter” or “tribe.” The Septuagint reads “a man.” The verse was read messianically in later Jewish and Christian tradition; the Dead Sea Scrolls cite it (for example, in the Damascus Document and 4QTestimonia), and the second-century leader Simeon bar Kosiba was called Bar Kokhba, “son of the star.”
Or “the borders.” Hebrew “the two sides of the head.”
Or “the sons of tumult.” Compare Jeremiah 48:45. Sheth may be a people’s name.
Hebrew qen, “nest,” is a wordplay on Qayin, “Kain,” the name of the Kenites’ ancestor in verse 22.
The meaning of verses 21–22 is uncertain. Asshur is Assyria, or possibly a tribe of that name (Genesis 25:3).

The Hebrew of verses 23–24 is very difficult. The Septuagint introduces this saying with “And he looked on Og.” Some scholars, revising the Hebrew, read “Who will live among the islands of the north?”
Kittim is Cyprus, and by extension the peoples of the western Mediterranean coasts.

verses.text: While Israel was staying at Shittim,{a} the people began to commit sexual immorality with the women of Moab.
They invited the people to the sacrifices of their gods, and the people ate and bowed down to their gods.
So Israel yoked itself to the Baal of Peor.{b} And the anger of Yahweh burned against Israel.
Yahweh said to Moses, “Take all the chiefs of the people and impale{c} them before Yahweh in the sun, so that the fierce anger of Yahweh may turn away from Israel.”
And Moses said to the judges of Israel, “Each of you kill those of his men who have yoked themselves to the Baal of Peor.”

Just then one of the Israelites came and brought a Midianite woman to his brothers, in the sight of Moses and in the sight of the whole congregation of the Israelites, while they were weeping at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
When Phinehas{d} son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, saw it, he rose from the midst of the congregation and took a spear in his hand.
He went after the man of Israel into the inner room{e} and pierced both of them, the man of Israel and the woman, through her belly. So the plague was stopped among the Israelites.
Those who died in the plague were twenty-four thousand.
Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,
“Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, has turned back my wrath from the Israelites, in that he was zealous with my zeal among them, so that I did not consume the Israelites in my zeal.
Therefore say, ‘Look, I am giving him my covenant of peace.
It will be for him and for his descendants after him a covenant of a permanent priesthood, because he was zealous for his God and made atonement for the Israelites.’”
The name of the slain man of Israel, who was killed with the Midianite woman, was Zimri son of Salu, leader of a father’s house of the Simeonites.
And the name of the Midianite woman who was killed was Cozbi daughter of Zur, who was head of the people of a father’s house in Midian.{f}
Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,
“Harass the Midianites and strike them down,

for they have harassed you with their schemes, with which they deceived you in the matter of Peor, and in the matter of Cozbi, the daughter of the leader of Midian, their sister, who was killed on the day of the plague in the matter of Peor.”{g}

notes.text: Shittim means “acacia trees.”
Baal means “lord” or “master,” the title of a Canaanite storm god. Baal of Peor was the god worshiped at Peor (compare 23:28).
The meaning of the Hebrew verb is uncertain; it may mean to impale, to hang, or to expose with broken limbs. The Septuagint reads “make an example of them.”
Phinehas is an Egyptian name meaning “the Nubian.”
The Hebrew word qubbah, found only here, probably refers to a tent shrine or an inner chamber.
Zimri means “my protection” or “my song.” Salu is of uncertain meaning. Cozbi perhaps means “deceitful” or “voluptuous.” Zur means “rock.”
In the Hebrew text, the sentence “After the plague” forms verse 19 of chapter 25. In English Bibles it begins 26:1.

verses.text: After the plague, Yahweh spoke to Moses and to Eleazar son of Aaron the priest, saying,
“Take a census of the whole congregation of the Israelites, from twenty years old and upward, by their fathers’ houses, all in Israel who are able to go out to war.”
So Moses and Eleazar the priest spoke with them in the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho, saying,
“Take a census of the people from twenty years old and upward,” as Yahweh had commanded Moses.{a} These were the Israelites who came out of the land of Egypt:
Reuben, the firstborn of Israel. The descendants of Reuben: Hanoch, the clan of the Hanochites; Pallu, the clan of the Palluites;
Hezron, the clan of the Hezronites; Carmi, the clan of the Carmites.
These were the clans of the Reubenites, and those counted of them were 43,730.
The son of Pallu was Eliab.

The sons of Eliab were Nemuel, Dathan, and Abiram. These are the Dathan and Abiram, chosen from the congregation, who contended against Moses and Aaron in the company of Korah, when they contended against Yahweh,
and the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them up together with Korah, when that company died, when the fire consumed two hundred fifty men, and they became a warning.
But the sons of Korah did not die.
The descendants of Simeon by their clans: Nemuel, the clan of the Nemuelites; Jamin, the clan of the Jaminites; Jachin, the clan of the Jachinites;
Zerah, the clan of the Zerahites; Shaul, the clan of the Shaulites.
These were the clans of the Simeonites, 22,200.
The descendants of Gad by their clans: Zephon, the clan of the Zephonites; Haggi, the clan of the Haggites; Shuni, the clan of the Shunites;
Ozni, the clan of the Oznites; Eri, the clan of the Erites;
Arod, the clan of the Arodites; Areli, the clan of the Arelites.
These were the clans of the descendants of Gad, according to those counted of them, 40,500.
The sons of Judah were Er and Onan, and Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan.
The descendants of Judah by their clans were: Shelah, the clan of the Shelanites; Perez, the clan of the Perezites; Zerah, the clan of the Zerahites.
The descendants of Perez were: Hezron, the clan of the Hezronites; Hamul, the clan of the Hamulites.
These were the clans of Judah, according to those counted of them, 76,500.
The descendants of Issachar by their clans: Tola, the clan of the Tolaites; Puvah, the clan of the Punites;
Jashub, the clan of the Jashubites; Shimron, the clan of the Shimronites.
These were the clans of Issachar, according to those counted of them, 64,300.
The descendants of Zebulun by their clans: Sered, the clan of the Seredites; Elon, the clan of the Elonites; Jahleel, the clan of the Jahleelites.
These were the clans of the Zebulunites, according to those counted of them, 60,500.
The descendants of Joseph by their clans: Manasseh and Ephraim.
The descendants of Manasseh: Machir, the clan of the Machirites; and Machir fathered Gilead; Gilead, the clan of the Gileadites.
These were the descendants of Gilead: Iezer,{b} the clan of the Iezerites; Helek, the clan of the Helekites;
Asriel, the clan of the Asrielites; Shechem, the clan of the Shechemites;
Shemida, the clan of the Shemidaites; Hepher, the clan of the Hepherites.
Zelophehad son of Hepher had no sons, but only daughters. The names of the daughters of Zelophehad were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.{c}
These were the clans of Manasseh, and those counted of them were 52,700.
These were the descendants of Ephraim by their clans: Shuthelah, the clan of the Shuthelahites; Becher, the clan of the Becherites; Tahan, the clan of the Tahanites.
And these were the descendants of Shuthelah: Eran, the clan of the Eranites.
These were the clans of the descendants of Ephraim, according to those counted of them, 32,500. These were the descendants of Joseph by their clans.
The descendants of Benjamin by their clans: Bela, the clan of the Belaites; Ashbel, the clan of the Ashbelites; Ahiram, the clan of the Ahiramites;
Shephupham,{d} the clan of the Shuphamites; Hupham, the clan of the Huphamites.
The sons of Bela were Ard and Naaman: Ard, the clan of the Ardites; Naaman, the clan of the Naamites.
These were the descendants of Benjamin by their clans, and those counted of them were 45,600.
These were the descendants of Dan by their clans: Shuham, the clan of the Shuhamites. These were the clans of Dan by their clans.
All the clans of the Shuhamites, according to those counted of them, were 64,400.
The descendants of Asher by their clans: Imnah, the clan of the Imnites; Ishvi, the clan of the Ishvites; Beriah, the clan of the Beriites.
Of the descendants of Beriah: Heber, the clan of the Heberites; Malchiel, the clan of the Malchielites.
And the name of the daughter of Asher was Serah.
These were the clans of the descendants of Asher, according to those counted of them, 53,400.
The descendants of Naphtali by their clans: Jahzeel, the clan of the Jahzeelites; Guni, the clan of the Gunites;
Jezer, the clan of the Jezerites; Shillem, the clan of the Shillemites.
These were the clans of Naphtali by their clans, and those counted of them were 45,400.
These were those counted of the Israelites, 601,730.{e}
Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,
“Among these the land is to be divided as an inheritance according to the number of names.
To a large tribe you are to give a larger inheritance, and to a small tribe you are to give a smaller inheritance. Each is to be given its inheritance in proportion to those counted of it.
But the land is to be divided by lot. They are to inherit according to the names of the tribes of their fathers.
Their inheritance is to be divided by lot between the larger and the smaller.”
These were those counted of the Levites by their clans: Gershon, the clan of the Gershonites; Kohath, the clan of the Kohathites; Merari, the clan of the Merarites.
These were the clans of Levi: the clan of the Libnites, the clan of the Hebronites, the clan of the Mahlites, the clan of the Mushites, the clan of the Korahites. And Kohath fathered Amram.
The name of Amram’s wife was Jochebed daughter of Levi, who was born to Levi in Egypt. And she bore to Amram Aaron and Moses and Miriam their sister.
To Aaron were born Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.
But Nadab and Abihu died when they offered unauthorized fire before Yahweh.
Those counted of them were 23,000, every male from a month old and upward. For they were not counted among the Israelites, because no inheritance was given to them among the Israelites.
These were those counted by Moses and Eleazar the priest, who counted the Israelites in the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho.
But among these there was not a man of those counted by Moses and Aaron the priest, who had counted the Israelites in the Wilderness of Sinai.
For Yahweh had said of them, “They will surely die in the wilderness.” Not one of them was left, except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.

notes.text: The words “Take a census of the people” are not in the Hebrew, which is abrupt here; they are supplied from verse 2.
In Joshua 17:2 the name is Abiezer.
Mahlah perhaps means “weakness”; Noah (not the same name as Noah of the flood), “movement”; Hoglah, “partridge”; Milcah, “queen”; Tirzah, “pleasing.”
So the traditional Hebrew text. Some manuscripts and ancient versions read “Shupham” (compare the clan name); Genesis 46:21 has Muppim.
The total is slightly less than the 603,550 of the first census (1:46). On the meaning of the figures, see the note at 1:46.

verses.text: Then the daughters of Zelophehad son of Hepher, son of Gilead, son of Machir, son of Manasseh, of the clans of Manasseh son of Joseph, came forward. The names of his daughters were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
They stood before Moses, before Eleazar the priest, before the leaders, and before the whole congregation at the entrance of the tent of meeting, and said,
“Our father died in the wilderness. He was not among the company of those who gathered themselves together against Yahweh in the company of Korah, but he died for his own sin, and he had no sons.
Why should the name of our father be taken away from his clan because he had no son? Give us a possession among our father’s brothers.”
Moses brought their case before Yahweh.{a}
And Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,
“The daughters of Zelophehad are right in what they are saying. You must give them a possession as an inheritance among their father’s brothers and transfer the inheritance of their father to them.
And you are to speak to the Israelites, saying, ‘If a man dies and has no son, then you are to transfer his inheritance to his daughter.
If he has no daughter, then you are to give his inheritance to his brothers.
If he has no brothers, then you are to give his inheritance to his father’s brothers.

And if his father has no brothers, then you are to give his inheritance to the nearest relative of his clan, and he is to possess it. It is to be for the Israelites a statute and rule, as Yahweh commanded Moses.’”
Yahweh said to Moses, “Go up into this mountain of Abarim{b} and see the land that I have given to the Israelites.
When you have seen it, you also will be gathered to your people, as Aaron your brother was gathered,

because you rebelled against my command in the Wilderness of Zin when the congregation quarreled, failing to treat me as holy at the waters before their eyes.” (These are the waters of Meribah of Kadesh in the Wilderness of Zin.)
Moses spoke to Yahweh, saying,
“Let Yahweh, the God of the spirits of all flesh, appoint a man over the congregation,
who will go out before them and come in before them, who will lead them out and bring them in, so that the congregation of Yahweh may not be like sheep that have no shepherd.”
So Yahweh said to Moses, “Take Joshua son of Nun, a man in whom is the Spirit,{c} and lay your hand on him.
Have him stand before Eleazar the priest and before the whole congregation, and commission him in their sight.
You are to put some of your authority on him, so that the whole congregation of the Israelites may obey.

He is to stand before Eleazar the priest, who will inquire for him by the judgment of the Urim{d} before Yahweh. At his word they will go out, and at his word they will come in, both he and all the Israelites with him, the whole congregation.”
Moses did as Yahweh commanded him. He took Joshua and had him stand before Eleazar the priest and before the whole congregation,
and he laid his hands on him and commissioned him, as Yahweh had directed through Moses.{e}

notes.text: In the traditional Hebrew text the final letter of “their case” (mishpatan) is written larger than normal.
Abarim means “regions beyond,” the mountain range east of the Dead Sea that includes Mount Nebo (Deuteronomy 32:49).
Or “spirit.”
The Urim and Thummim were objects kept in the high priest’s breastpiece and used to learn God’s will (Exodus 28:30). The meaning of the words is uncertain; Urim may be related to ’or, “light.”
At this point the Samaritan Pentateuch adds material drawn from Deuteronomy 3:21–22, in which Moses encourages Joshua. The Dead Sea Scroll 4QNumᵇ preserves a similar expansion. See the note at 10:10.

verses.text: Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,
“Command the Israelites and say to them, ‘You are to take care to present to me at its appointed time my offering, my food for my offerings by fire, a pleasing aroma to me.’
And you are to say to them, ‘This is the offering by fire that you are to present to Yahweh: male lambs a year old without blemish, two each day, as a regular burnt offering.
You are to offer the one lamb in the morning, and the other lamb you are to offer at twilight,{a}
with about 2 quarts of fine flour for a grain offering, mixed with about 1 quart of oil from pressed olives.{b}
It is a regular burnt offering, which was instituted at Mount Sinai as a pleasing aroma, an offering by fire to Yahweh.
Its drink offering is to be about 1 quart for each lamb. In the holy place you are to pour out a drink offering of strong drink{c} to Yahweh.
The other lamb you are to offer at twilight. Like the grain offering of the morning and its drink offering, you are to offer it as an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to Yahweh.
“‘On the Sabbath day: two male lambs a year old without blemish, and about 4 quarts of fine flour{d} for a grain offering, mixed with oil, and its drink offering.
This is the burnt offering of every Sabbath, besides the regular burnt offering and its drink offering.
“‘At the beginnings of your months{e} you are to present a burnt offering to Yahweh: two young bulls, one ram, and seven male lambs a year old without blemish;
also about 6 quarts of fine flour for a grain offering, mixed with oil, for each bull; and about 4 quarts of fine flour for a grain offering, mixed with oil, for the one ram;
and about 2 quarts of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering for each lamb,{f} for a burnt offering of pleasing aroma, an offering by fire to Yahweh.

Their drink offerings are to be about 2 quarts of wine for a bull, about 1⅓ quarts for a ram, and about 1 quart for a lamb.{g} This is the burnt offering of each month throughout the months of the year.
Also one male goat for a sin offering to Yahweh is to be offered, besides the regular burnt offering and its drink offering.
“‘On the fourteenth day of the first month (in March–April){h} is Yahweh’s Passover.
And on the fifteenth day of this month is a festival. For seven days unleavened bread is to be eaten.
On the first day there is to be a holy assembly. You must not do any ordinary work.
You are to present an offering by fire, a burnt offering to Yahweh: two young bulls, one ram, and seven male lambs a year old. See that they are without blemish.
Their grain offering is to be of fine flour mixed with oil: about 6 quarts for a bull and about 4 quarts for the ram;
about 2 quarts you are to offer for each of the seven lambs;
also one male goat for a sin offering, to make atonement for you.
You are to offer these besides the burnt offering of the morning, which is for a regular burnt offering.
In this way you are to offer daily, for seven days, the food of the offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to Yahweh. It is to be offered besides the regular burnt offering and its drink offering.
And on the seventh day you are to have a holy assembly. You must not do any ordinary work.
“‘On the day of the firstfruits,{i} when you present a new grain offering to Yahweh at your Festival of Weeks, you are to have a holy assembly. You must not do any ordinary work.
You are to present a burnt offering as a pleasing aroma to Yahweh: two young bulls, one ram, and seven male lambs a year old;
also their grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil, about 6 quarts for each bull, about 4 quarts for the one ram,
and about 2 quarts for each of the seven lambs;
also one male goat, to make atonement for you.
Besides the regular burnt offering and its grain offering, you are to offer them and their drink offerings. See that they are without blemish.’”

notes.text: Hebrew “between the two evenings,” probably the time between sunset and dark. So also in verse 8. See the note at Exodus 12:6.

Hebrew “a tenth of an ephah of fine flour … a quarter of a hin of beaten oil,” about 2.2 liters of flour and 0.9 liter of oil. An ephah was about three-fifths of a bushel (22 liters), and a hin about 1 gallon (3.7 liters); standards varied. So also with the drink offering in verse 7.
Hebrew shekar, a fermented drink, possibly beer.
Hebrew “two-tenths,” about 4.4 liters.
Hebrew “heads of your months,” the new moon at the beginning of each lunar month.
Hebrew “three-tenths … two-tenths … a tenth” of an ephah, about 6.6, 4.4, and 2.2 liters. The same amounts are given in verses 20–21, 28–29, and in chapter 29.
Hebrew “half a hin … a third of a hin … a quarter of a hin,” about 1.9, 1.2, and 0.9 liters.
First month: Abib, later called Nisan, of the spring-start religious calendar. Because the months were lunar, the dates fall in different parts of March and April from year to year.
The Festival of Weeks (Shavuot) was held fifty days after the offering of the first sheaf (Leviticus 23:15–16), in the third month, Sivan (in May–June).

verses.text: “‘On the first day of the seventh month (in September–October){a} you are to have a holy assembly. You must not do any ordinary work. It is a day for you to blow trumpets.{b}
You are to offer a burnt offering as a pleasing aroma to Yahweh: one young bull, one ram, and seven male lambs a year old without blemish;
also their grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil, about 6 quarts for the bull, about 4 quarts for the ram,
and about 2 quarts for each of the seven lambs;
with one male goat for a sin offering, to make atonement for you;

besides the burnt offering of the new moon and its grain offering, and the regular burnt offering and its grain offering, and their drink offerings, according to the rule for them, a pleasing aroma, an offering by fire to Yahweh.
“‘On the tenth day of this seventh month (in September–October){c} you are to have a holy assembly, and you are to humble yourselves.{d} You must not do any work.
You are to present a burnt offering to Yahweh as a pleasing aroma: one young bull, one ram, and seven male lambs a year old. See that they are without blemish.
Their grain offering is to be of fine flour mixed with oil, about 6 quarts for the bull, about 4 quarts for the one ram,
and about 2 quarts for each of the seven lambs;
also one male goat for a sin offering, besides the sin offering of atonement, and the regular burnt offering and its grain offering, and their drink offerings.
“‘On the fifteenth day of the seventh month (in September–October){e} you are to have a holy assembly. You must not do any ordinary work, and you are to celebrate a festival to Yahweh seven days.
You are to present a burnt offering, an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to Yahweh: thirteen young bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old. They are to be without blemish.
Their grain offering is to be of fine flour mixed with oil, about 6 quarts for each of the thirteen bulls, about 4 quarts for each of the two rams,
and about 2 quarts for each of the fourteen lambs;
also one male goat for a sin offering, besides the regular burnt offering, its grain offering, and its drink offering.
“‘On the second day: twelve young bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old without blemish,
with their grain offering and their drink offerings for the bulls, for the rams, and for the lambs, according to their number, by the rule;
also one male goat for a sin offering, besides the regular burnt offering, its grain offering, and its drink offerings.{f}
“‘On the third day: eleven young bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old without blemish,
with their grain offering and their drink offerings for the bulls, for the rams, and for the lambs, according to their number, by the rule;
also one male goat for a sin offering, besides the regular burnt offering, its grain offering, and its drink offering.
“‘On the fourth day: ten young bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old without blemish,
with their grain offering and their drink offerings for the bulls, for the rams, and for the lambs, according to their number, by the rule;
also one male goat for a sin offering, besides the regular burnt offering, its grain offering, and its drink offering.
“‘On the fifth day: nine young bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old without blemish,
with their grain offering and their drink offerings for the bulls, for the rams, and for the lambs, according to their number, by the rule;
also one male goat for a sin offering, besides the regular burnt offering, its grain offering, and its drink offering.
“‘On the sixth day: eight young bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old without blemish,
with their grain offering and their drink offerings for the bulls, for the rams, and for the lambs, according to their number, by the rule;
also one male goat for a sin offering, besides the regular burnt offering, its grain offering, and its drink offering.
“‘On the seventh day: seven young bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old without blemish,
with their grain offering and their drink offerings for the bulls, for the rams, and for the lambs, according to their number, by the rule;
also one male goat for a sin offering, besides the regular burnt offering, its grain offering, and its drink offering.
“‘On the eighth day you are to have a solemn assembly.{g} You must not do any ordinary work.
You are to present a burnt offering, an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to Yahweh: one bull, one ram, and seven male lambs a year old without blemish,
with their grain offering and their drink offerings for the bull, for the ram, and for the lambs, according to their number, by the rule;
also one male goat for a sin offering, besides the regular burnt offering, its grain offering, and its drink offering.

“‘These you are to offer to Yahweh at your appointed festivals, in addition to your vowed offerings and your freewill offerings, for your burnt offerings, your grain offerings, your drink offerings, and your peace offerings.’”
So Moses told the Israelites everything that Yahweh had commanded Moses.{h}

notes.text: Seventh month: Tishri, also called Ethanim (1 Kings 8:2), of the spring-start religious calendar. Because the months were lunar, the dates fall in different parts of September and October from year to year. In later Jewish tradition this day became Rosh Hashanah, the civil New Year.
Hebrew teru‘ah, a day of loud blasts, probably on the ram’s horn. Compare Leviticus 23:24.
The Day of Atonement (Yom Kippur). See Leviticus 16:29–34; 23:26–32.
Or “afflict yourselves,” traditionally understood as fasting.
The Festival of Booths (Sukkot). See Leviticus 23:33–43.

In verses 19, 31, and 33 the Hebrew has small irregularities of spelling (“their drink offerings,” “its drink offerings,” “by their rule”). Ancient rabbis noticed that the extra letters spell mayim, “water,” and took this as a hint of the water libation at the Festival of Booths.
Hebrew ‘atseret, a closing assembly.
In the Hebrew text, verse 40 is numbered 30:1.

verses.text: Moses spoke to the heads of the tribes of the Israelites, saying, “This is what Yahweh has commanded.{a}
When a man makes a vow to Yahweh, or swears an oath to bind himself by a pledge, he must not break his word. He must do according to all that comes out of his mouth.
“When a woman makes a vow to Yahweh and binds herself by a pledge, while she is in her father’s house in her youth,
and her father hears her vow and her pledge by which she has bound herself and says nothing to her, then all her vows will stand, and every pledge by which she has bound herself will stand.
But if her father opposes her on the day that he hears of it, none of her vows or her pledges by which she has bound herself will stand. And Yahweh will forgive her, because her father opposed her.
“If she marries a husband while under her vows or any rash utterance of her lips by which she has bound herself,
and her husband hears of it and says nothing to her on the day that he hears, then her vows will stand, and her pledges by which she has bound herself will stand.
But if, on the day that her husband hears of it, he opposes her, then he makes void her vow that was on her and the rash utterance of her lips by which she bound herself. And Yahweh will forgive her.
(But any vow of a widow or of a divorced woman, anything by which she has bound herself, will stand against her.)
“If she vowed in her husband’s house or bound herself by a pledge with an oath,
and her husband heard of it and said nothing to her and did not oppose her, then all her vows will stand, and every pledge by which she bound herself will stand.

But if her husband makes them void on the day that he hears them, then whatever comes out of her lips concerning her vows or concerning her pledge will not stand. Her husband has made them void, and Yahweh will forgive her.
Any vow and any binding oath to humble herself,{b} her husband may confirm, or her husband may make void.

But if her husband says nothing to her from day to day, then he confirms all her vows or all her pledges that are on her. He has confirmed them, because he said nothing to her on the day that he heard of them.
But if he makes them void after he has heard of them, then he will bear her iniquity.”
These are the statutes that Yahweh commanded Moses concerning a man and his wife, and concerning a father and his daughter while in her youth in her father’s house.

notes.text: In the Hebrew text, verses 1–16 are numbered 30:2–17.
Or “to afflict herself,” perhaps by fasting.
